6653702698961890320~raw: "Errant strokes corrected. Parameters adjusted." She once tried to fit the curves of the sea into her artwork, extracting the form and spirit of water and analyzing the scattered specks of foam. Time and again, countless waves bloomed from her brush, but none was the one she had imagined. "I wish to paint for all: not to trace their footsteps, but to illustrate their path forward." With a sweep of her brush, she brought shelter to famished children. With a wash of ink, she mended the rifts between the sky and the earth with her strokes. And her furthest stroke pierced the canvas of this world, extending into the vast cosmos. For countless yesterdays, she painted the future for others... The pale and the bleak, imbued with the color of hope. Looking back, every stroke she laid down also shaped the "Pearl" within her heart.

When the doctor found the wounded girl, she was clinging to a machine that had stopped working, with all sorts of parts filling her pocket.
She took the girl back to her clinic and treated the wounds.
Drops of sweat slowly rolled down the girl's cheek, but she remained silent and her hands didn't stop fiddling the machine.
To the doctor, the way the girl was attached to the machine was very much like how she was attached to her patients who needed help.
So the doctor did not try to comfort the girl nor did she nag her about being more careful; but rather, she sat down with her to give her a moment of peace.
